title: A "Fair" Duel
subtitle: A showdown for the future of a shining star.

trails.title: Ownerless Notebook
trails.description: Includes muck, traces of blood, and expensive means of preserving one's dignity.

content.text: A Notebook Covered in Mud and Blood

Page One

Duels are not for the purpose of self-■■■■■■■■■■—they are to demonstrate one's chiv■■■■,
to uphold the honor of one's lord or oneself.

Do not initiate ■■■■■■■■ over trivial matters.

———————————————————————

A duel! You don't want to miss it!

When one party is insulted, they may issue a challenge to the insulting party.

The challenged party must either accept or ■■■■■■ like a little rat, humil■■■■■ in front of everyone.

Challenge by mail ■■■■■■■■■, by throwing down the gauntlet (silk or leather), or by verbal ■■■■■■■■.

———————————————————————

Maybe a verbal one is better ... 

Page Two

Both parties of the duel should bring an assistant and a doctor.

After agreeing on the terms and conditions of defeat (perhaps when one party is ■■■■■■■■■■■■■, or one party di■■, ■■■■■■■■ shall stop after firing three shots), the duel can officially begin.

———————————————————————

Must so many people be involved?

items.text: A "Fair" Duel

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Good day. I would like to check the date of a novel.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Yes, it is The Man Without Qualities, by Robert Musil.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Oh. I see, I see ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: What did they say?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Just as I remembered it ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The novel was completed in 1930, the word "Kakania" was also created by Robert Musil.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Kakania should not be a nickname for anyone in 1914.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: It doesn't belong to this era.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: She could be with Manus Vindictae, or, at least is associated with their people.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: What's more ... When we were at the Secession Building, I "read" that painting, The Salvation.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It seemed ... out of place compared to the other paintings. Theophil may have applied a new technique on The Salvation, a more daring kind, audacious, even.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But these are only subtleties ... I can't be too certain. I was interrupted by that strangely speaking gentleman, so I didn't get everything.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Another thing, its content reminds me of the symbol of "The Circle."
Marcus rummages through the bookcase, finding the pamphlet tucked within the thick register.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: This twisting circle resembles the circles in The Salvation.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Heinrich called them magical circles, one next to another. They must be more than just circles, I think ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Was he demonstrating the madness of passion? But the lines are clean. Perhaps the purity of eternity? No, the circles are too twisted for that ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Or, was he just representing a primitive state of being ...?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I don't understand any of it.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: So, this must be art.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hahaha, ma'am. You're funny sometimes.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: ...? I wasn't joking.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Based on what we know, we can't be sure if this group of young arcanists and the Manus are connected. But we all know that the latter is eager to win over the cynical, revolutionary youth.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: You did well, Marcus.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The important figures of "The Circle"—Isolde, Heinrich, and even the late Theophil—we have made contact with them all.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Only this Kakania ... What does the intel say about her?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Kakania, also known as Ms. Klara, inherited her arcane skills from her family. She's able to reflect people's thoughts in a mirror. She was once a medical student, but dropped out halfway through.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: These days, she shows up at various social events as a psychiatrist, which the Foundation tries to prohibit because she doesn't have a license.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: And she is also ... an activist.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: An activist?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: According to Mr. Heinrich, she is meeting with a doctor named Schwartz today.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Schwartz ... The family doctor Karl mentioned.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Let's try our luck there.

items.speaker: Notary
items.text: Now then, Ms. Klara, Mr. Schwartz.

items.speaker: Notary
items.text: Only three weapons are allowed in the duel—the army knife, the sword, and the pistol.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I will leave the choice to Dr. Schwartz, for he has more experience in these duels than I do. It's an honor to fight you, and I look forward to ending your winning streak.

items.speaker: Dr. Schwartz
items.text: Not so much an honorable thing for me.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Excuse me ... Please ...
Hofmann extends her hand, mercilessly cleaving a path through the crowd.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Pardon me. What is happening?

items.speaker: Passerby I
items.text: A duel, ma'am!

items.speaker: Passerby I
items.text: Just as Dr. Schwartz was demonstrating his therapy, Ms. Klara barged right in! They were arguing, and this is how they decided to end it.

items.speaker: Passerby I
items.text: To ensure fairness of the duel, the combat must happen within 48 hours of the challenge ... But I've never seen one take place on the spot.

items.speaker: Passerby II
items.text: Well, I hope they know what they're doing. I don't want to get caught as collateral damage.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: That green dress ... So she is Kakania! What do we do? If she gets injured, our mission will ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Don't worry about people in their time. It is their life to live.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Never intervene if you don't know the exact consequences of your actions. The course of history is more important than our investigation.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: This is investigator Greta Hofmann.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: What ...? Hold on.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I'll be right back.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Where are you going?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The Field Agent Squad needs to speak to me. This won't take long.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I will leave this to you. Remember what I said, Marcus.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Yes, madam.
Hofmann turns toward the Baroque wooden door made of mahogany, before her figure disappears amidst the crowd.
Only her still-unfledged assistant remains.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Leaving this to me, to me, to me ...
Marcus recites it to herself as a mantra, attempting to slow her racing heart.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Breathe, Marcus! There's nothing to be nervous about. You can't be an assistant forever. There will come a day when you're all on your own.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Just like at the Secession Building, I only have to watch her. If I end up talking to Ms. Kakania, I'll just pretend to be an ordinary employee of the Foundation ... Easy!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: You used to do well on your own, when you were reading in the lighthouse and the forest ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Mm, Dr. Schwartz ... Three times he has been involved in duels, and three times he has won—impressive! This time, he's still going for the pistol.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But ... Ms. Kakania does not have an assistant. And she has only one witness in this duel. This is not right. Why did she agree to this?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: She's being reckless. Even an arcanist should have at least one assistant in a duel.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Dr. Schwartz's assistant brought them a pair of pistols ... FN Model 1910. Hmm, is that a right weapon for a duel?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It's too crowded here. I can't see ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No, the pistol given to Ms. Kakania ... something's wrong with it.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The bullets ... Her life is in danger if the duel begins!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But Madam Hofmann warned me about the consequences of intervention ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: What if, what if, I just go and talk to her as an employee of the Foundation branch, like I did at the Secession Building?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: So far, Heinrich has been difficult to communicate with, while Mr. Karl doesn't want us to get in touch with Ms. Isolde.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ms. Kakania is the only person who is both a friend of Theophil and associated with "The Circle." But I have to be careful with this name.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: If she is indeed one of the Manus Vindictae, I will be jeopardizing this mission by going near her ... But wait! She doesn't know that I'm from the headquarters, so she probably will talk to me.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But how do I know she doesn't know my identity? What if Mr. Karl is not to be trusted? And what if Mr. Karl and she are in this together? Their names both start with a "K" ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: What am I thinking?
Marcus patting her cheeks with an unaware gusto, drawing side glances from the others present.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Stop, stop! I'm not on the Flannan Isles anymore. I can't waste my day on endless thoughts!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Remember what Madam Hofmann said, think of the immediate mission. I have to prevent Kakania from getting killed in the duel. She has the clues about Theophil that I need ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Never intervene if you don't know the exact consequences of your actions ...
A long, deep breath.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I have assessed the risks, madam.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I will not stand by and watch this happen ... even if I don't know the consequences!

items.speaker: Dr. Schwartz
items.text: I need to make this clear to you. Not only have you hindered Ms. Dittarsdorf from getting the treatment she needs, but you have repeatedly defamed me.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, I can only admit that you're right if you have to call a different academic perspective slander.

items.speaker: Dr. Schwartz
items.text: "A different academic perspective" ... ?! Do you really think Freud and his petty tricks are "academic"?

items.speaker: Dr. Schwartz
items.text: One could hardly find a worse insult to science than this!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Is that so? Do you really mean that? Rumor has it that you taught the military the method of hypnosis for a price. Do you wish to clear things up here?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Hah, your silence is a resounding "yes." Tell me, why did you please the ministers with these "petty tricks," but not with your "most advanced" electrotherapy you've been touting?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Do you harbor negative feelings towards Mr. Freud because of his open rejection of hypnosis?

items.speaker: Dr. Schwartz
items.text: ... What does any of this have to do with you?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Many things, Mr. Schwartz. Your behavior has greatly undermined the interests of arcanists, who are your own people.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Not to mention that hypnosis is a violation of a patient's free will!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And I have reason to believe that this duel is entirely personal. I must make it clear that your wife's appointment with me has nothing to do with the rumors of your ... lackluster performance in the bedroom.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm not the real enemy, Mr. Schwartz. The gossipmongers and the tabloid writers are!

items.speaker: Dr. Schwartz
items.text: You, you ...

items.speaker: Notary
items.text: Are both duelists ready?

items.speaker: Dr. Schwartz
items.text: Perfectly ready.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm ready too—

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No! She's not!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ms. Kakania needs another minute!
Their collective gaze causes her voice to tremble slightly.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Err, ahh, the crowd ... shoot me, I want to go home ... Why oh why did you apply for this mission, Marcus ...
Despite her mental turmoil, she extends her hand, attempting to ascend with some dignity intact, or at least without resorting to crawling.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I-I am Ms. Kakania's assistant. I'm here to ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Sorry to interrupt, miss. But the last time I checked, I couldn't possibly afford a St. Pavlov Foundation member to be my aide.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ah! Darn it, I forgot about my badge ...
Kakania retracts her pistol, twirling it around her finger.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: So the Foundation is trying to intervene. Don't worry, Ms. Foundation staff! Look around, we're doing it the human way—no arcane skills involved!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The head of the Foundation branch should not be your role model. Mind you, you're giving up a part of your integrity for taking his Krones! A terrible deal indeed.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Besides, we're using human guns! We don't need the Foundation's license to use these. I'm not doing anything against the Foundation's rules, am I?
The Browning pistol spins once more in a perfect circle.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If it's urgent, can we wait until after the duel? Please stand back, the bullets can't tell the difference between friend and enemy.
Marcus is again interrupted by the rapid-fire speech of the other party.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Please don't use that gun! The bullets in it are dangerous!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... What?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text:
The bullets are wrong! The gun will burst if you pull the trigger!
Sir, I demand that the gun be checked ...
Kakania grips the half-turned gun tightly, before deftly removing the magazine.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The size of these bullets ...
A cold bead of sweat drips down her spine.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I need an explanation, Mr. Schwartz. I thought you had at least the integrity of a gentleman.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The bullets in my gun are wrong. If I pull the trigger, as Ms. Foundation here said, the barrel will burst.

items.speaker: Passerby II
items.text: A bursted barrel? I remember now. That Anton boy lost the duel to Schwartz for the same reason! Did Schwartz do something to his gun, too? And was the guard in on it too?

items.speaker: Dr. Schwartz
items.text: D**n! ... This is defamation! I have never ... !

items.speaker: Vienna Guard
items.text: Freeze! Who is dueling here?!

items.speaker: Passerby I
items.text: Ahhh! The guards are here!

items.speaker: Passerby III
items.text: Hey, don't step on my dress!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Not good! Madam Hofmann has not come back yet. Madam Hofmann ...!
The young assistant is engulfed within the chaotic crowd.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Hey, miss! The helpful Ms. Foundation employee!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ms. Kakania?
The green-clad pistoleer extends her hand.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Don't stand there ... Come here!
Kakania grabs the shy assistant's hand, pulling her into a fierce embrace without a second word.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Aahh!
Kakania leaps, alighting herself onto the window frame with the lightness of a bird.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Okay, this is a quiet road ... We're going to jump, Ms. Foundation. Three, two, one ... Here we go!
TO BE CONTINUED…
